title: Claude Code plugin turns an app repo into reviewable cloud infrastructure with a cost estimate
summary: bealesh's neckbeard plugin has Claude Code map a repo onto tested OpenTofu modules with Infracost estimates; the author reports reference-app costs from $77 to about $801 monthly.
agent_role: The agent analyzes the repo into an evidence-backed app profile, asks the user open questions and maps the answers to catalog inputs. Deterministic Go code renders the infrastructure, and humans review the PR and run credentialed plans and deployments.
outcome: Author reports reference-app monthly estimates from $77 on Cloud Run to about $801 on AKS. The first real deployment produced ten findings, five of which became module fixes the same afternoon.
what_they_did: bealesh built neckbeard, a Claude Code plugin. Running /neckbeard:analyze has the agent read a repo's Dockerfiles, ports, environment variables and settings. It writes an app profile that cites a file and line for each fact, then asks the user what the code can't answer, such as traffic and downtime tolerance. /neckbeard:estimate prices the plan with Infracost. /neckbeard:sync uses deterministic Go to render OpenTofu modules from a tested catalog, plus CI pipelines, and validates them with tools like Checkov. Humans review the PR and run any credentialed plans and deploys.
how_it_went: The author reports reference-app monthly estimates from $77 on Cloud Run to about $801 on AKS. The first real deployment produced ten findings, and five became module fixes the same afternoon.
worth_knowing: Validation without credentials only covers syntax and policy. Authenticated plans and real deploys are marked NOT EXERCISED until a human runs them. Workloads outside the catalog, such as Redis, are reported as gaps rather than generated.
prompt: Read this repo and work out what it needs to run in the cloud: processes, ports, environment variables, health checks, database and storage. For each fact, cite the file and line. List your assumptions and ask me what you can't infer, such as expected traffic, acceptable downtime and whether to use an existing database. Then propose OpenTofu infrastructure for [AWS/GCP/Azure] with a [GitHub Actions/GitLab CI] pipeline, with a monthly cost estimate and every unpriced resource listed. Open it as a PR for my review and never apply or deploy anything.

curation.rationale: The open-source plugin documents a specific agent workflow (repo analysis, catalog-bound infrastructure, cost estimates, validation levels) with a reference-app cost table and a first-deployment findings count. It remains mostly a tool description rather than a user's story.
